title: רב אסי
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: (a) Rav’s student-colleague, needing his received tradition, not reasoning. Tosafot, Bava Batra 62a: Assi and Kahana like student-colleagues. Shabbat 146b: Rav avoided cushions out of respect for Kahana and Assi, Rashi: his student-colleagues. Niddah 36b: Shila bar Avina ruled like Rav on labor and blood, declaring niddah, etc. As Rav died he told Assi, “Go tell him privately” that she is wholly pure; if disobedient, “draw him” by proofs. Assi understood “force him” by excommunication. After Rav’s death: “Retract; Rav retracted.” Shila: “He would have told me, his student.” Refusing, he was banned. “Do you not fear fire?” “I am Issi ben Yehudah, also called Issi ben Gur Aryeh, Issi ben Gamliel, and Issi ben Mahalalel.” Tosafot: Pesachim’s tanna has those names, plus Yosef the Babylonian, Yosef of Hutzal; only Issi names like Assi appear here. See Issi ben Akiva; Tosafot, Yoma 52b. Chiddushei Aggadot: his father’s names marked his virtues. (How the same virtues as the tanna’s father? Halakhot Ketannot, cited above, suggests that people may have changed their fathers’ names during persecution; Assi must have reused Issi’s alternatives. But why tell Shila his father’s names?) Father’s merit would preserve him; Issi hints at a bronze mortar, impervious to rot, Rashi. “I am Shila bar Avina, an iron pestle breaking bronze.” Assi fell ill and died. Shila told his wife, “Prepare my shrouds, lest he speak against me before Rav,” and died. Myrtle flew between their biers—customary bier myrtle, Rashi. Shalshelet Hakkabbalah 34a says blood fell: an error. They concluded the sages made peace. That work: “Shila and Ashi, not the Talmud’s compiler, hated each other.” Wrong: Assi, not Ashi. Echad Dinei Mamonot; Megillah 5a; Kiddushin 45b: Rav respected Assi’s concern; Rabbenu Tam nevertheless rules like Rav.

(b) Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 2, mishnah 8: Yisa ascended, had a haircut, and went toward the bath. A scoffer struck his neck. A ruler was judging a robber: “Who was with you?” Seeing the scoffer laugh, the robber named him; arrested, he confessed a murder and was hanged. Apparently Rav Assi, Babylonian who ascended: he was in the Land. Kiddushin 31b: his elderly mother wanted jewelry; he provided it. A husband? “We shall seek one.” “As handsome as you.” He left for the Land. Hearing she followed, he asked Yochanan about leaving the Land: forbidden; to meet Mother? “I do not know.” Later: “Assi, resolved to leave? May God return you safely,” etc. Hearing her coffin came, “Had I known, I would not have left.” (Sedeh Yehoshua, Jerusalem Berakhot 25c: this Yisa question is the Bavli’s Rav Assi story, as Yuchasin: “Rav Assi, Rabbi Assi the priest, Yisa in Jerusalem Talmud, Ammi’s colleague, both Yochanan’s students.” Under Yisa he equates him with Rav Assi. Shlomo Sirilio likewise, citing the wedding-attendants story in Haya Kore: Bavli Rav Assi, Jerusalem Yisa; a priest, Hannizakin’s distinguished priests Ammi and Assi, subordinate to Rav; also Mi Shemeto. End quotation. Confused! Rav Assi is Yisi, but not a priest; Rabbi Assi was a priest. Yisi is Rav Assi, not Rabbi Assi: two men, the latter a priest.) Pesachim 113a: do not live where the head is Asi—meaning you, named Rav Assi, should not be head and lose study to public affairs; not Rashbam’s physician interpretation. Tosafot, Bava Batra 110a; see Ammi.

(c) Kahana’s colleague, Tosafot, Shabbat 45b. “Rav Assi visited Rav Assi’s house for Mar bar Rav Ashi’s wedding.” Yuchasin separates an entry, thinking this the late Rav Ashi. Mistaken: Mar was the early Ashi’s son; read “visited Rav Ashi’s house,” Ketubbot 8a. Chullin 19a: Huna in Assi’s name; Tosafot: Kahana’s colleague, not Rabbi Assi, Huna’s junior; likewise Shabbat 45b. Huna from Assi, Chullin 20a; Bava Batra 126, beginning of a. Tosafot, Berakhot 34a: Halakhot Gedolot favors Assi, Huna like his student; Rosh agrees. Rav says, etc.; Assi says, etc. Huna—or Chiyya bar Rav—objected to Assi; Rav told his student and son, “Did I not tell you not to reverse it?”, Ketubbot 48b. Rosh, Asarah Yuchasin, favors Assi as greater than Shmuel, who would not enter before him, Merubbeh 80, beginning of b. Not age: Shmuel, Rabbi’s physician, Bava Metzia 85b, was older than Kahana. Jerusalem Talmud calls Kahana a boy on coming to Yochanan, all the more Assi, younger still, Kahana usually listed first. End quotation. Bava Kamma 99, beginning of a: Rashi favors Shmuel; see why. Sefer Keritot and Yavin Shemuah make Assi Shmuel’s student, relied on by Kenesset Yechezkel 8b in one ruling. All erred: he was not Shmuel’s student but greater.

(d) Rav Assi asked Rabbi Abba bar Mammal. Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Assi visited Rabbi Abba of Haifa. Was it because Rabbi Assi was Rabbi Yochanan’s student? Shabbat 45b. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana and Rabbi Assi from Ulla, end of Eikhah’s opening discourse. Rabbi Abba bar Binyamin bar Chiyya contemporary. Rabbi Yisa from Avduma of Haifa, Jerusalem Berakhot 4, mishnah 4. Abbahu, colleague of Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi, Yevamot 65b. Rav Adda bar Ahavah to Yisa, Jerusalem Kiddushin 1:7. Rav Oshaya from Rav Assi, Shabbat 18a; a case of Oshaya’s sling, Assi consulted. In Hoshaya’s name, Jerusalem Sukkah 1, end of halakhah 1. Rav Acha bar Rav Avya before Rav Assi; Acha bar Ava, Acha bar Azza, Acha bar Chanina in Assi’s name. Rabbi Acha the elder; Achi, Rabbi Assi’s colleague; Ila from Yisa (see Hila). Assi in Elazar’s name. Rav Assi to Rav Ashi: “Manasheh teaches,” Bekhorot 36, beginning of a; “Did not Abbahu say in Yochanan’s name?”, Zevachim 6a; Sukkah 8a. Ashyan bar Yakim asked Yisa. Rav Bibi from Rav Assi. Berekhiah says Ravsa, Chazit, “Who is this ascending”; Mattanot Kehunnah: shortened Rav Assi. Gamliel Zuga asked Yisa. Geniva from Rav Assi; Rav Huna likewise; Hamnuna in Assi’s name. Hillel bar Valles (see there). Zeira, Rabbi Assi’s student; Ze'ira to Yisa. Chiyya Beruna; Chiyya bar Rav objected (see above). Chiyya bar Abba before Yochanan and Assi, calling them children and disputing. Chelbo and Yisa; Chelbo of Teva; Chama bar Ashi; Yisa in his name. He asked Chama bar Yosef; Chanina bar Yosef and Assi asked Yochanan. Rav Assi from Chanina, Menachot 50b; Rav Chinena from Assi, Tamid 31b. Chinena: “He holds”; Assi from Yochanan. Rav Yehudah from Assi, Shabbat 22a; Yevamot 16, end of b, Rav Assi, but Asheri’s Ashi is erroneous; Gittin 64b, Rabbi Assi. Rav Assi from Rav Yehudah, Bava Metzia 43a. Yehudah bar Shila from Assi; they asked Yochanan. Rav Yehudah bar Ulla in Rabbi Assi’s time. Assi from Yochanan, Rosh Hashanah 12b; Yoma 84b; Kiddushin 13a. Ta'anit 29b: Rav Assi from Yochanan—perhaps Rabbi Assi. Rabbi Assi asked Yochanan, Nedarim 82b. He said to Yochanan, “When master says law, may we act?” “Not until I say practical law,” Bava Batra 130, end of b. Assi from Yehoshua ben Levi, Chullin 98a; see Tanchum. Yisa in his name, Jerusalem Berakhot 3, mishnah 4; Bavli 29, beginning of b. Yehoshua Deromaya; Rav Yehoshua bar Rav Idi visited Rav Assi. Rav Assi heard a great man, Yose bar Chanina, Bava Kamma 42b. Rav Yosef from Assi from Yochanan. Yaakov from Assi from Mana (see above); Yaakov bar Acha in his name; Yaakov bar Zavdi asked him. Assi from Yannai, Niddah 12a; Yannai from Assi, Eikhah Midrash 57b. Assi before Yitzchak Nappacha; Yitzchak, his colleague. Yirmeyah asked Assi, Gittin 44a; Assi to Yirmeyah, Chullin 21a. Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba visited Rav Assi. Levi bar Chayta of Megevila before him. Rav Assi in Manasheh’s name; Meyasha bar Yirmeyah’s; Mana bar Tanchum’s. Mana, his student. Mesharshya bar Rav Ammi to Rav Assi; Nachman bar Yitzchak from Assi; Nechemyah bar Ukvan; Rav Sama bar Rav Assi; Simon. Rav Amram—Rami bar Yechezkel sent to him for a report from Rav Assi. In Pedaya’s name, Jerusalem Nazir 6:9:6 [cited here as 6:10]. Pinchas; Pashpasha. Rava bar Natan and Rabbi Assi. Rava bar Rabbah bar Rav Huna from Rav Assi. Rav Assi told Rabbah, “My teacher, you say so?”, Bava Batra 155a; see Tosafot. Rabbah bar bar Chana before Rabbi Assi and Rabbi Ammi, Chullin 106a. Assi from Rabbah bar Yirmeyah; Assi said Rabbi [א״ר; referent unresolved], Bekhorot 56. Rami bar Yechezkel (see Rav Amram). Rami bar Abba, his father-in-law, from Rav Assi; Rami bar Chama from Rav Assi. Shmuel bar Ba asked Yisa, Jerusalem Nazir, end of chapter 2. Assi in Shmuel bar Yitzchak’s name, and he in Assi’s. Rav Assi from Resh Lakish, Shabbat 45, end of b. Heilprin proposes Rabbi Assi, citing 63, end of a. The checked edition reads Rabbi Assi at 45b and Rav Assi at 63a. In Shabbatai’s name. Rav Sheshet from Rav Assi. Tanchum from Assi; Tanchum bar Mari in Yose’s name. Know that Jerusalem-Talmud Yisa is Rav Assi.
